title: LLM Security Threat Model
requirement_text: The system must have an explicit LLM security threat model covering: prompt injection (direct and indirect), jailbreak attempts, sensitive-data leakage, API-key misuse, quota/resource exhaustion, metadata leakage, unsafe tool use, excessive agency, context poisoning, supply-chain risk, and unsafe output handling.

title: Canonical REQ ID Format
requirement_text: The LLM security requirements register must use stable REQ IDs with prefix REQ-LLMSEC- and zero-padded sequential numbers starting from 001.

title: AI-BOM Provider Inventory
requirement_text: The system must maintain an AI-BOM provider inventory documenting provider protocol, endpoint scope, operator control, credential mode, retention assumption, and data boundary for all LLM provider instances.
notes: Provider inventory with openai-compatible protocol classification

title: RAG/Vector Memory Not Applicable
requirement_text: RAG/vector memory is not currently used by k9b. Diagnosis context is provided via snapshot artifacts passed directly to LLM prompts. Future introduction requires documented permission scoping, PII scanning, sanitization, retention policy, and audit trail.
notes: Evidence: No RAG implementation in codebase

title: MCP/Tool-Server Integrations Not Applicable
requirement_text: MCP/tool-server integrations are not currently used by k9b. Tool access is hardcoded; diagnosis tools are operator-provided kubectl/helm commands. Future introduction requires tool allowlisting, scoped credentials, dangerous operation blocking, policy tests, audit logging, and sandboxing.
notes: Evidence: No MCP implementation in codebase

title: Additional Self-Managed Inference Not Applicable
requirement_text: Additional self-managed inference provider instances beyond the currently documented openai-compatible loopback instance are not currently used. Future addition requires meeting provider boundary requirements, credential isolation, sanitization, endpoint scope documentation, operator control classification, retention policy, and data boundary classification.
notes: Evidence: Only openai-compatible loopback inference supported
